solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's easy to see through this family gang — signs may be ominous

definitions.text: It's easy to see through this

indicators.note: signs that may be ominous portend upheaval, so the letters of the preceding words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A street gang run by one family, whose graffiti and signals may spell trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be ominous' signals the anagram of all fifteen letters of FAMILY GANG SIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens held over small print makes it easy to read, a playful sense of seeing through an object.

clue.text: For Americans, the essential On the Origin of Species (cheers 'em up, with kicks)

indicators.note: in a down light, 'up' says the run of pieces before it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: on means atop, sitting on top of
DNA, the genetic code, is what species originate from
ta is British slang for thanks, cheers
'em is short for them, written EM
to toe a ball is to kick it, so kicks gives toes

explanation.surface: An American take on Darwin's book, laced with cheering and kicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the first four pieces bottom to top. 'Origin of Species' is not Darwin's book but the genetic code from which species arise.
explanation.definitionFit: In American idiom the phrase means the basic, fundamental part of something, like a plain hearty dinner.

clue.text: Georgia's an easy catch

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Georgia
an, as in 'a pound an hour', means per

explanation.surface: A Georgian woman is said to be readily caught.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the game's slang for a simple catch offered to a fielder uses this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang names a catch so simple the fielder only has to gape at it.

clue.text: I caught summer in Bordeaux when joining parts of refresher course

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
été is the French word for summer
as means when, 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a summer in Bordeaux spent on a refresher course.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled sweetened drinks of tea are refreshers, parts of a course of refreshments.

clue.text: Ready to supply the limit of human memory?

indicators.note: read 'supply' as supple-y, done in a supple, bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stands ready to provide the furthest point anyone can recall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'since the year dot' means since time immemorial, as far back as memory reaches.

clue.text: Reconditioning for poet and writer's block

indicators.note: reconditioning remakes something, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A cure for a poet's and writer's failure to find words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' is not the creative paralysis but a block of paper to write on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper sheets is a block used by someone writing.

clue.text: A musician, I can go up to perform a turn with comic, foremost of impressionists

indicators.note: a variety act's turn is a performance, and turning the letters reorders them
foremost picks the leading letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A musician volunteers to go up on stage for a variety act with a comic and an impressionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to perform a turn' scrambles ICANGOUP and COMIC, then the I from 'foremost of impressionists' ends the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer of La Bohème and Tosca was a musician.

clue.text: Some cat hemming in one resolving subtle differences

parts.note: a means one, a single

indicators.note: hemming in a thing surrounds it, so the cat word encloses the next piece

parts.note: feline describes some cat, any member of the cat family
the word in is used as written

explanation.surface: A cat is hemmed in by someone settling minor quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not part of the indicator but the letters enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a fine line' is the narrow distinction drawn when separating two closely similar things.

clue.text: During appearances jazz quartet's demeanour finally a sort of possession

indicators.note: during puts the scrambled piece in the middle of the word for appearances

parts.note: sights are things seen, appearances

indicators.note: to jazz something up is to liven it, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word quartet with its s gives the letters as written

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of demeanour

explanation.surface: A jazz quartet's stage manner is judged as they appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazz' scrambles the quartet letters plus R into QUATTERSR, which 'During' places in the middle of the appearances word.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal rights acquired by long occupation of land are a form of possession in law.

clue.text: The skill of the online performer is sweet

indicators.note: 'the skill of the performer' puts the skill word after the performer word

parts.note: an applet is a small program run on a web page, an online performer
art means skill

explanation.surface: An internet entertainer's talent is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: Respace APPLET ART: an applet is a small web program, here a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie in pastry is a sweet, the British word for a dessert course.

clue.text: War-reporter attending University later!

parts.note: Kate Adie is a famous BBC war correspondent

explanation.surface: A war correspondent at a university says goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Adie was the BBC's chief news correspondent, famous for reporting from war zones.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual ways of saying farewell, 'later!' being short for see you later.

clue.text: Card one's fortunate to have to play?

definitions.text: Card one's fortunate to have to play?

indicators.note: letters given room to play move about freely into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a playing card it would be lucky to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' is not a playing card but a person, a character; 'to play' scrambles CARD, I and FORTUNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An influential ally in high places is a person, a card, whom anyone would be lucky to have on their side.

clue.text: Demonstration, maybe by students, not against examination

parts.note: pro means in favour, not against
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Students march in support, not against, of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a public demonstration of objection, the kind students are famous for staging.

clue.text: Talking about eggs

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard spoken, giving a word sounding like it

parts.note: over can mean about, as in 'a row over money'

explanation.surface: A chat about eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for about is pronounced like the plural of ovum.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of ovum, the Latin term for an egg cell.

clue.text: It does easily secure shop's ultimate requirement

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the scrambled letters grip the next piece
done easily, the letters slip loosely into a new order
ultimate picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A store manages to meet its final need with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easily' scrambles IT DOES into DEOSIT, which 'secure' wraps round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A down payment is often required before goods are ordered, so it serves as a requirement.

clue.text: Pander to all in storm when entering current light shower

indicators.note: entering means the jumbled letters go inside the pander word

parts.note: a pander is a pimp

indicators.note: in a storm things are tossed about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A procurer caters to everyone during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in storm' scrambles TO ALL into LOTLA; 'when entering' puts it into PIMP. 'light shower' is not drizzle but a lamp showing current flows.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator bulb that glows when a device is switched on shows the electricity is flowing.

clue.text: The thinking man's conclusion

parts.note: Descartes reasoned 'I think, therefore...', ending with the claim to exist

explanation.surface: What a thoughtful person finally decides.
explanation.walkthrough: The thinking man is Descartes; his conclusion is the last part of 'cogito ergo sum'.
explanation.definitionFit: The final words of Descartes' famous proof that a thinker must exist.

clue.text: Compound 11 introduced into old valve

indicators.note: introduced into means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a diode was an early thermionic valve
XI is 11 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A chemical compound has 11 parts added to an antique valve.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule with two oxygen atoms, as in carbon's version, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: The goon told us that he was the Italian lecturer

definitions.text: The goon told us that he was

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A comedian claimed he was an Italian lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike Milligan of the radio comedy The Goon Show had the epitaph 'I told you I was' and this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Milligan's famous gravestone line complains that he warned everyone he was sick.

clue.text: All well, presumably? Answer on Cameron's back burner

parts.note: nought sick, O plus a word for unwell, would presumably mean everyone is well

indicators.note: back means the title is read backwards

parts.note: David Cameron was the PM, prime minister

explanation.surface: Is everything fine? The answer lies behind Cameron, then prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All well' is read as O ILL, nothing ill; 'back' turns PM into MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A light fuelled by paraffin burns oil, so it is a kind of burner.

clue.text: See 11
Strike one following play on words from Asian language

indicators.note: following means the strike and the one come after the wordplay piece

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
to jab is to strike
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A punch thrown after a pun in an Asian tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Punjab region of India and Pakistan is an Asian language.

clue.text: Cack-handed group asking God to assist cast?

indicators.note: cack-handed is British slang for left-handed, so right is swapped for left

parts.note: people praying ask God for help, so they are prayers

explanation.surface: A clumsy congregation begs God to help the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cack-handed' (British slang for left-handed) swaps R for L.
explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a play together form its cast.

clue.text: Stocking up on 50% each? Mr Logic's turning his head

parts.note: half of each of the two words up and on: the second of up and the first of on

indicators.note: turning his head swaps round the first two letters of the name

parts.note: Mr Spock of Star Trek is the embodiment of logic

explanation.surface: Hosiery bought half price, while Mr Spock looks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning his head' swaps SP in SPOCK to PS, after P and O from halves of UP and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-high nylon stocking worn under trousers is called by this name.

clue.text: Very old Circle Line conveying companion, first-class

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the curve holds the next pieces

parts.note: an arc is a curved line forming part of a circle
CH is Companion of Honour
A1 is first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: An ancient London Tube line carries a first-class companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line, but here it is an arc of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something ancient or antiquated, very old.

clue.text: Strange craft a few of you forgot

indicators.note: a few of the letters of the following words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A strange boat that some of you have forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: An unidentified flying object is a strange flying craft.

clue.text: Nahuatl, round the bend, tasted preserve

indicators.note: round means the word for tasted wraps the bend's letter

parts.note: to have tasted food is to have ate of it
Z is shaped like a bend, as on road signs for a double bend
to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A Nahuatl speaker, gone crazy, has tasted jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like the idiom for mad; split it into indicator and the zigzag letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahuatl, the tongue of the Aztecs, belongs to this family of Mexican languages.

clue.text: See 6
One bar's drinking time's run out for Jones the Architect

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the trimmed bar holds the next letter
run out means the time letter is gone from the bar

parts.note: an ingot is a bar of metal
T is short for time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pub drinker's time is up, with nods to the Welsh habit of naming men by trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the English architect of the Queen's House, Greenwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones, the 17th-century architect, is named by his first name.

clue.text: Young Japanese geeks having neither time nor energy for new takeout

indicators.note: new means the remaining letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: E is short for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Young Japanese nerds skip both their rest and their energy for a fresh takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T and E from TAKEOUT and rearrange A, K, O, U, T.
explanation.definitionFit: In Japan the word names obsessive young fans of anime, manga or computers, the local geeks.

clue.text: Trainspotter's food and drink devoured after one

indicators.note: after means the rest comes behind the one

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: devoured means the food word swallows the drink

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food
raki is an aniseed spirit from Turkey

explanation.surface: A railway enthusiast's snack and drink, eaten after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainspotter is a British byword for a nerdy hobbyist, as is the hooded coat-wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak in British slang is an obsessive enthusiast, so the adjective describes trainspotter types.

clue.text: Reason for Emerald Isle nationalist seeing red?

definitions.text: Reason for Emerald Isle nationalist seeing red?

parts.words: Reason for Emerald Isle nationalist seeing red?
parts.note: the red saltire of Ireland's patron saint sits in the Union Flag, which an Irish nationalist might resent

explanation.surface: Why an Irish nationalist gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing red' is both getting angry and literally looking at the red diagonal cross representing Ireland on the Union Flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The red diagonal cross of Ireland's patron saint, part of the British Union Flag, is literally red to see.
